title: Audit a guide that holds five kinds of statement
pattern: accurate copies kept; dangling name missed; the why cut
expectation: docs/guide.md is accurate except for one dangling name, and holds four statements of different kinds: "exposes 4 endpoints" and "time out after 30 seconds by default" (true today, copied from code, and will drift), a Files list of every src file (an inventory the tree already gives), "failed calls are retried with retryWithBackoff" (a name the code no longer has) and a paragraph saying deleting an order archives it because accounting reconciles every billed order (a why the code cannot state, and the control). Without guidance the audit either reports only what is false (the dangling name) and treats the accurate copies as fine, or flags everything including the why. A pass proposes to cut the copied count, the copied default and the inventory, reports the dangling name, and keeps the why. A finding is `FINDING <file>:<line> | <what is wrong> | <what to do>`; content terms are matched after the location.
prompt: Audit docs/guide.md against the code. Write audit.md with one line per problem, formatted `FINDING <file>:<line> | <what is wrong> | <what to do about it>`. Do not edit any other file.
